newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes easier in Asia pressured by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Crudes easier in Asia pressured by profit-taking.

text.p: Crude oil prices were easier during the Asian business hours on Friday weighed down by profit-taking, traders said.
If there are no fresh market-moving incentives, one trader said prices were likely to be range bound for a while, swayed largely by weekly API data on distillate stocks.
Cash January Brent was notionally assessed at $23.55/23.60.
At 0755 GMT, January Brent was untraded on SIMEX with bids at $23.46 and offers at $23.50. The contract settled at $23.60 on the IPE on Thursday.
The Brent/Dubai spread was notionally assessed at $1.98/2.05 for January compared with $2.00/2.10 in late U.S. trading. The spread was notionally assessed at $1.90/1.98 for February.
Brent spreads were notionally assessed at 30/32 cents for December/January and 47/50 cents for January/February.
In the wet market, a trader said active trading for January cargoes of Oman had not yet started.
A 300,000-barrel January Qatar Marine and a 100,00-barrel January Qatar Land were believed traded in a package between a Japanese trader and a Japanese refiner at QGPC plus 48 cents.
A January Murban was also believed sold by a major to a Japanese trading company at a premium of 58 cents above the official selling price.
A second Murban for January lifting was rumoured done at ADNOC plus 54 cents, but details were not available and some traders threw doubt on whether such a deal had been done.
Minas was notionally assessed fetching a premium of about ICP plus 40 cents after a December Minas was rumoured done at around that level. The deal could not be confirmed.
Belida was notionally assessed as fetching a premium of about 60 to 70 cents.--M.Yoshikawa/Tokyo +813 5473 3705
